program.eligibility: Early-stage and scaling life-science companies, with a focus on cell and gene therapy

strategy.thesis: Wet-lab and office campus co-located with GSK's UK R&D facility, created to bring academia, biotech and pharma together to accelerate healthcare research; a hub for cell and gene therapy in the UK's 'Golden Triangle'.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Co-located with GSK R&D facility; incubator + accelerator space totalling c.5,500 sqm of laboratory, office and networking space.

summary.en: UK life-science campus co-located with GlaxoSmithKline's Stevenage R&D site, offering rent-free incubator lab space to early-stage start-ups and larger accelerator lab/office space, with a strategic focus on cell and gene therapy.

sources.title: Stevenage Bioscience Catalyst: Empowering Innovation
sources.supports: existence, GSK co-location, founding year, lab/office space
sources.quote: The Bioscience Catalyst opened in 2012 and is co-located with GlaxoSmithKline's UK R&D facility and provides both Incubator and Accelerator spaces, totalling c.5,500 sq m of laboratory, office and networking space.

sources.title: Member profile: Stevenage Bioscience Catalyst
sources.supports: focus on cell and gene therapy, largest cluster in Europe claim
sources.quote: It supports up to 7 early-stage start-ups rent-free for 6 months in the Incubator. One of the key areas of focus is cell and gene therapy technologies and the Campus is at the centre of the largest cluster within Europe.

program.location: BioCity Nottingham, BioCity Scotland (Newhouse), Alderley Park (Cheshire)

strategy.thesis: Life-sciences real-estate and venture-building group providing wet-lab and office incubation space plus business support/accelerator programmes across multiple UK campuses, descended from the original BioCity brand founded 2003 in Nottingham.

summary.en: UK life-sciences real-estate and venture-building company (rebranded from BioCity Group after a 2021 acquisition by Harrison Street and Trinity Investment Management) that operates wet-lab incubation campuses including BioCity Nottingham, BioCity Scotland and the Alderley Park accelerator.

verification_notes: BioCity Nottingham (est. 2003) is the UK's largest bioscience incubation centre; the parent company rebranded to 'We Are Pioneer Group' / 'Pioneer Group' after a joint venture between Harrison Street and Trinity Investment Management acquired BioCity Group and merged it with Trinity's real-estate business. Exact rebrand date not confirmed in sources searched.

sources.title: BioCity becomes We are Pioneer
sources.quote: a joint venture between investor management firm Harrison Street and Trinity Investment Management acquired BioCity Group, which had run successful accelerators for nearly 20 years, and combined with Trinity's real estate business to form We Are Pioneer Group.

sources.title: Member profile: We Are Pioneer Group Limited
sources.supports: current operator of BioCity Nottingham, business support model
sources.quote: Pioneer Group provides holistic business support to life science entrepreneurs at scaleup, growth and startup stages. BioCity Nottingham is the UK's largest bioscience innovation and incubation centre, now run by Pioneer Group, a specialist life sciences real estate and venture building company.

program.location: MAxL incubator, IZB (Innovation and Start-up Center for Biotechnology), Martinsried, Munich, Germany
program.eligibility: Pre-seed and early-stage biotech/healthtech startup teams from Bavaria and beyond

strategy.thesis: Commissioned by the Bavarian state government as the central network organization for Munich/Bavaria's biotech cluster; operates the MAxL wet-lab incubator to give pre-seed teams shared bench space and structured coaching.

summary.en: Munich and Bavaria's official biotech cluster management organization, which runs the MAxL (Munich Accelerator Life Sciences & Medicine) incubator offering roughly 900 sqm of shared wet-lab and cell-culture space to pre-seed biotech and healthtech founders at the IZB in Martinsried.
summary.local: Die zentrale Netzwerkorganisation für die Biotechnologiebranche in München und Bayern, im Auftrag des Freistaats Bayern; betreibt den MAxL-Inkubator mit Laborflächen im IZB Martinsried.

sources.title: BioM opens new startup incubator MAxL
sources.supports: lab space size, workstation count, focus
sources.quote: Spanning approximately 900 square meters in the Biotechnology Innovation and Start-up Center (IZB), MAxL aims to set new standards for the biotechnology industry in Bavaria. The laboratory area offers 18 immediately usable laboratory workstations, a fully equipped shared laboratory, and a cell culture area.

sources.title: Biotech Cluster Munich-Martinsried
sources.supports: role as Bavaria's biotech cluster organization
sources.quote: BioM is the central network organization for the biotechnology sector in Munich and Bavaria, commissioned by the Bavarian Ministry of Economic Affairs.

program.location: Cochin Hospital campus (Paris Santé Cochin), Paris, France

strategy.thesis: Health-focused incubator co-founded by Paris-Descartes University, ESSEC, École Centrale Paris and INSERM to develop medications, medical devices and innovative care; based at Cochin Hospital with L1-L3 wet labs.

summary.en: Paris incubator specialized in medicines, medical devices and care innovation, founded in 2000 by Paris-Descartes University, ESSEC, Ecole Centrale Paris and INSERM; based at the Cochin Hospital campus (branded Paris Santé Cochin) with ~7,300 sqm of L1-L3 wet labs across two buildings, described as Europe's largest health-focused business nursery by resident count.
summary.local: Incubateur parisien spécialisé dans le médicament, le dispositif médical et le soin innovant, fondé en 2000 par l'Université Paris-Descartes, l'ESSEC, l'École Centrale Paris et l'INSERM, situé sur le site de l'hôpital Cochin.

sources.title: Parisbiotech Santé
sources.quote: The incubator was founded in 2000 by Paris-Descartes University, ESSEC, École Centrale Paris, and INSERM. The permanent facilities of Paris Biotech were inaugurated on June 5, 2003.

sources.title: Paris Biotech Santé : un incubateur et une pépinière de choix pour les start-ups santé
sources.quote: The building has 3,530 m² of laboratories (with level L1, L2, and L3 laboratories) and offices made available to companies. The surface area was doubled in 2018 with the construction of a second adjacent building of 3,782 m². With 53 companies and startups in its facilities, Paris Santé Cochin is today Europe's largest health nursery.

program.location: Multiple European sites: Paris (Hôtel-Dieu), Paris-Saclay, Heidelberg, Berlin, Munich (BioLabs|TUM, opening 2026)
perks: Flexible, on-demand fully licensed wet-lab benches

strategy.thesis: For-profit shared wet-lab and office coworking network for biotech startups, expanding a US-proven model (bench fees, no equity) into major European biotech hubs.

summary.en: US-founded (Cambridge, MA, 2009) network of shared, fully licensed wet-lab and office coworking facilities for biotech startups that has expanded into Europe with sites in Paris (Hôtel-Dieu), Paris-Saclay, Heidelberg and Berlin, plus a new BioLabs|TUM site in Munich opening in 2026; membership is flexible with bench fees and no equity taken.

verification_notes: BioLabs is headquartered in Cambridge, MA, USA; included here because it operates dedicated wet-lab facilities across multiple European cities (France, Germany).

sources.title: Hôtel-Dieu, Paris, France | BioLabs
sources.quote: BioLabs Hôtel-Dieu is a collaborative wet lab and office coworking facility that is on demand, flexible, scalable, fully equipped and fully licensed.

sources.title: BioLabs Heidelberg, Germany
sources.quote: BioLabs Heidelberg is a collaborative wet lab and office coworking facility... located in the key biotech innovation cluster Rhine Neckar.

sources.title: New biotech hub BioLabs|TUM launched to foster start-ups
sources.quote: With 1800m² dedicated to laboratories, offices and event spaces, BioLabs | TUM will be a place of growth for young companies... anticipated to open in early 2026.

strategy.thesis: Corporate-run, on-campus incubator giving early-stage life-science startups lab and office space plus access to Bayer's research infrastructure and expertise, adjacent to Charité and Humboldt University.

summary.en: Bayer-operated wet-lab and office incubator on Bayer's Berlin research campus, hosting up to nine early-stage life-science companies in ~420 sqm of labs, connected to Charité hospital and Humboldt University research institutions.

sources.title: 35 European Biotech Incubators
sources.supports: lab space size, founding year, cohort
sources.quote: Bayer HealthCare CoLaborator™ - Host: Bayer HealthCare - Location: Berlin - Size: 800 m² (420 m² labs for nine companies) - Founded: 2014 - Focus: Startup life-science platforms aligned with Bayer

sources.title: The 14 Best Biotech Incubators for Startups in 2025
sources.quote: The Bayer CoLaborator offers office and laboratory space to companies at all stages of development and is located at the Bayer research campus in Berlin, this incubator is connected to prestigious research institutions such as the Charité hospital and the Humboldt University.

investment.raw: up to EUR 1.3M per start-up (pre-seed) and EUR 2.4M per project

strategy.thesis: Novo Nordisk Foundation-backed independent life-science incubator combining non-dilutive funding with wet-lab and office infrastructure to mature health-tech, therapeutics and bioindustrial research projects toward investable companies.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Operates ~3,500 sqm of state-of-the-art wet labs and office facilities at its Copenhagen headquarters (Copenhagen Bio Innovation Park).

summary.en: Independent Copenhagen incubator established in 2017 by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, offering early-stage health-tech, therapeutics and bioindustrial start-ups roughly 3,500 sqm of wet-lab and office space alongside non-dilutive funding of up to about EUR 1.3M (pre-seed) and EUR 2.4M (project); became an independent foundation in 2021 and received a DKK 5.5bn ($860M) commitment from Novo Nordisk Foundation to scale up.

sources.title: The Novo Nordisk Foundation establishes BioInnovation Institute as an independent foundation
sources.quote: The Novo Nordisk Foundation established the life science incubator BioInnovation Institute (BII) in 2017, with the purpose of advancing research, innovation, and entrepreneurship within the life sciences. In 2021, the BioInnovation Institute became an independent commercial foundation with a non-profit objective.

sources.title: Novo Nordisk BioInnovation Institute (BII) (Copenhagen)
sources.quote: BII, located in Copenhagen, Denmark, offers start-ups and early-stage projects... 2300 square-meters of state-of-the art labs... unique funding opportunities of up to EUR 1.3 million per start-up and EUR 2.4 million per project. More recently, BioInnovation Institute currently operates 3,500 square meters of laboratory and office facilities at its Copenhagen headquarters.

sources.title: Novo Nordisk Foundation invests $860M in Danish institute nurturing homegrown biotechs
sources.quote: The Novo Nordisk Foundation is investing 5.5 billion Danish kroner ($860 million) in the BioInnovation Institute (BII) to help scale up more homegrown biotechs and deep tech companies.

program.location: Alderley Park, Cheshire, UK (former AstraZeneca R&D campus)

strategy.thesis: 400-acre former AstraZeneca R&D campus converted into a life-science and tech innovation park with scalable chemistry/biology wet labs and an onsite accelerator (historically run by BioCity/Pioneer Group) for early-stage life-science companies.

summary.en: Life-science and tech innovation campus in Cheshire, run by Bruntwood SciTech on the former AstraZeneca R&D site, offering over 1 million sq ft of chemistry and biology wet-lab and office space from single-bench to 100,000 sq ft, plus an onsite life-science accelerator.

sources.title: Alderley Park Innovation Campus, Cheshire
sources.quote: Alderley Park is an internationally-recognised life science and tech campus located in Cheshire... over 1 million square feet of lab and office space across a 400-acre park... chemistry and biology labs of various sizes—from single benches to 100,000 sq. ft.

sources.title: 35 European Biotech Incubators
sources.quote: BioHub at Alderley Park - Location: Alderley Edge, Cheshire - Size: 86,000 sq ft (planned expansion to 300,000 sq ft) - Founded: 2013 (former AstraZeneca campus)

perks: Up to 12 months free communal lab space via Accelerate@Babraham

strategy.thesis: Cambridge-cluster bioscience campus hosting 60+ resident companies, offering staged wet-lab space (free communal LiveLabs for pre-seed via Accelerate@Babraham, dedicated ScaleLabs from 600 sq ft for growing companies) alongside academic and investor network access.

summary.en: Cambridge-area bioscience campus with over 60 resident companies, running the Accelerate@Babraham pre-seed programme (up to 12 months free communal lab space plus GBP 10K non-dilutive funding) and offering LiveLabs/ScaleLabs flexible wet-lab space for start-ups through scale-ups.

sources.title: Start-ups - Babraham Research Campus
sources.quote: Babraham Research Campus is a community designed for bioscience entrepreneurs to discover, innovate, grow and thrive... The Campus is home to over 60 companies, 2,000 employees and 300 academic researchers.

sources.title: About - Accelerate@Babraham
sources.supports: Accelerate@Babraham programme details, lab space, funding
sources.quote: The flagship incubator, Accelerate@Babraham, provides pre-seed founders with expert mentoring, an intensive taught programme, up to 12 months free communal lab space and non-dilutive funding to build commercial and scientific momentum.

sources.title: Flexible, Fully Fitted Laboratory Space
sources.quote: ScaleLabs offers dedicated wet lab and write-up spaces from 600 sq ft, designed for companies ready to establish independent operations and grow their teams.

strategy.thesis: France's first biocluster dedicated to genomics and biotechnology, pairing a business nursery with standard/L2 wet labs with the Shaker and Gene.IO acceleration programmes for innovative therapies, bioeconomy and digital genomics startups.

summary.en: France's first biocluster, based in Évry-Courcouronnes south of Paris, offering biotech start-ups a dedicated business nursery with L1/L2 wet-lab units (12-80 sqm) across roughly 42,000 sqm of managed real estate, alongside the Shaker and Gene.IO acceleration programmes.
summary.local: Premier biocluster français, situé à Évry-Courcouronnes, proposant une pépinière d'entreprises biotech avec laboratoires L1/L2 sur environ 42 000 m² de patrimoine immobilier géré par la SEM Genopole.

sources.title: The Genopole biocluster
sources.quote: The biocluster comprises five campuses, all located within three kilometers of Évry-Courcouronnes, with 42,000 m² managed by SEM Genopole.

sources.title: Biocluster dédié à l'incubation des startups de biotechnologie
sources.quote: the Genopole nursery provides an optimal environment for biotech startups, offering spaces from 12 m² to 80 m² with laboratories and offices designed to meet biotechnology research needs, including standard and L2 laboratories.

program.location: Tech Lane Ghent, plus Leuven and Brussels sites

strategy.thesis: Wet-lab incubator network run by Flemish life-sciences institute VIB, giving R&D-intensive biotech companies modular lab/office units near VIB's own research campuses in Ghent, Leuven and (newest) Brussels.

summary.en: Belgian life-sciences institute VIB's wet-lab incubator network: a ~6,000 sqm, 22-module facility in Ghent (Tech Lane) housing 10-15 R&D-intensive biotech companies, a sister L3-lab facility in Leuven, and a newer Bio Incubator Brussels site launched with Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB).

sources.title: Bio-Incubator
sources.quote: The VIB Bio-Incubator welcomes 10 to 15 biotech companies as a launchpad for those ready to make their mark in the Ghent region... offers 22 individual modules of 272 m² each, totaling approximately 6,000 m² of net operational space.

sources.title: VUB and VIB launch new Bio Incubator Brussels on VUB campus
sources.quote: VUB and VIB launch new Bio Incubator Brussels on VUB campus

strategy.thesis: Regional life-sciences incubator at Hasselt University's Diepenbeek campus, backed by Flemish investment company LRM, providing lab/office space to young, growing life-science companies.

summary.en: Life-sciences incubator on Hasselt University's Diepenbeek campus in Belgium, backed by regional investor LRM, offering over 3,600 sqm of wet-lab and office space across two development phases (2012-2014) for young growing healthcare/life-science companies.

verification_notes: Sourced from a single reputable industry list (GEN); could not independently verify current operating status or an official website in the budget available for this research pass.

sources.title: 35 European Biotech Incubators
sources.quote: BioVille - Host: LRM venture capital, Hasselt University - Location: Diepenbeek - Size: 3,600+ m² (two phases) - Founded: 2012–2014 - Focus: Young growing life sciences organizations

program.location: Medicon Village, Lund, Sweden (Medicon Valley cluster)

strategy.thesis: Scandinavia's largest life-science science park, built on a converted former AstraZeneca R&D site, hosting the SmiLe wet-lab business incubator that gives entrepreneurs shared cell/bacterial-culture and protein-purification lab infrastructure within the Medicon Valley cluster.

summary.en: Life-science research park in Lund, Sweden, created in 2010 from former AstraZeneca R&D buildings and now home to 180+ organizations across roughly 65,000 sqm of lab space; its on-site SmiLe Incubator offers about 1,700 sqm of shared, fully-equipped wet labs to life-science start-ups as part of the Medicon Valley cluster.

sources.title: Situated within one of Europe's strongest life science clusters
sources.quote: The total area available for letting within Medicon Village amounts to around 132,000 m², of which laboratories account for about 65,000 m², making it the largest science park in Scandinavia focusing on life science.

sources.title: SmiLe Incubator
sources.quote: SmiLe is a life science business incubator based in Medicon Village in Lund, Sweden... offers a unique infrastructure with well-equipped laboratories – including cell and bacterial culturing, protein purification, chemical and biochemical analyses, in total at 1,700 m² area.

sources.title: Medicon Village
sources.quote: The park was created as a transformation of former AstraZeneca buildings in 2010 and now employs more than 2,800 people in over 180 organisations.

program.location: Oslo Cancer Cluster Innovation Park, co-located with Oslo University Hospital and the Cancer Registry of Norway

strategy.thesis: Norway's primary oncology innovation cluster, co-locating an incubator of roughly 30 start-ups with private and shared molecular/cell-biology wet labs alongside Oslo University Hospital and the Cancer Registry of Norway to foster clinician-researcher-startup collaboration.

summary.en: Norway's leading oncology-focused innovation cluster in Oslo, co-located with Oslo University Hospital and the Cancer Registry of Norway, running an incubator of about 30 start-ups with private and shared molecular/cell-biology wet labs; named one of Europe's Leading Start-up Hubs for 2025 by the Financial Times and Statista.

sources.title: Facilities
sources.quote: Oslo Cancer Cluster is Norway's primary oncology innovation cluster with a named General Manager, an on-site incubator of approximately 30 startups, and co-location with Oslo University Hospital and the Cancer Registry of Norway. The Incubator Labs follow a distinctive model, which offers both private laboratories and fully equipped shared laboratories.

sources.title: A top start-up hub in Europe
sources.quote: A new special report from the business publication Financial Times and research company Statista highlights Oslo Cancer Cluster Incubator as one of Europe's Leading Start-up Hubs 2025, for the second year in a row.

strategy.thesis: Spain's first science park, run jointly by the University of Barcelona and the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, providing biomedical (plus environmental, IT and agri-food) wet-lab and office space for spin-offs and startups.

summary.en: Spain's first science park (1997), operated by the University of Barcelona and Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, offering roughly 60,000 sqm of biomedical, environmental, IT and agri-food wet-lab and office space to research spin-offs and startups.
